# How AI Strengthens Alignment From Vision To Execution

In this post, we’ll break down how AI strengthens alignment from strategy to delivery, and how different roles,leaders, project managers, product owners, and Scrum Masters,can harness AI to close the gap between intent and impact.

Written by**[Gowtham](/authors/gowtham)**

Updated**10 Aug, 2026**

Reading time**7 min read**

Turning a vision into execution has always been the hardest part of leadership. Anyone can set a bold direction, but aligning teams, decisions, and actions so that every step contributes to that vision is where organizations struggle. This is where Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a major improvements. AI doesn’t just automate tasks, it provides clarity, insights, and alignment so that leaders, teams, and stakeholders stay focused on what really matters.

In this post, we’ll break down how AI strengthens alignment from strategy to delivery, and how different roles, leaders, project managers, product owners, and Scrum Masters, can harness AI to close the gap between intent and impact.

---

## Why Alignment Breaks Between Vision and Execution

Even the most visionary organizations face challenges:

* **Miscommunication of goals**: What leaders envision often gets diluted as it travels down the hierarchy.
* Shifting priorities: Teams work on initiatives that feel urgent but don’t connect back to strategy.
* Lack of real-time feedback: By the time leadership realizes execution is off-track, months of effort are already wasted.
* Data overload: Decision-makers are drowning in metrics but lack meaningful insights.

AI addresses these gaps not by replacing human decision-making, but by enhancing clarity, speeding up insights, and ensuring continuous alignment across teams.

---

## AI as the Bridge Between Vision and Execution

AI acts as a connective layer, linking strategic intent with ground-level execution. Here’s how:

1. **Clarity at the Top**  
    Leaders can use AI-driven dashboards to see whether strategic objectives are progressing as intended. Instead of static reports, they get predictive insights that highlight risks before they escalate.
2. Consistent Communication  
    Natural Language Processing (NLP) tools can translate strategy into clear, role-specific tasks. For example, an AI system can convert a high-level objective like *“Improve customer experience”* into measurable backlog items for product teams.
3. Real-Time Adjustments  
    Machine learning algorithms detect execution drift early. If delivery outcomes don’t align with customer feedback or business KPIs, AI signals the need for a pivot.
4. Data-Driven Transparency  
    AI makes progress visible across all layers of an organization. Teams don’t just see their own tasks, they understand how their work ladders up to the bigger picture.

---

## How Leaders Use AI to Drive Alignment

Executives and change agents face the constant challenge of making strategic priorities stick. AI supports them in three ways:

* **Strategic Forecasting**: AI predicts which initiatives will deliver the most business value, helping leaders prioritize.
* Influence Mapping: Tools identify which stakeholders need to be aligned to avoid bottlenecks.
* Culture Insights: Sentiment analysis from employee feedback surfaces cultural misalignments that can derail execution.

For leaders and change agents, certifications like [AI for Agile Leaders & Change Agents](../artificial-intelligence/ai-for-agile-leaders-change-agents-certification) provide structured learning on how to use AI to strengthen alignment in transformation programs.

---

## How Project Managers Align Execution With Strategy Using AI

Project managers deal with scope creep, shifting timelines, and cross-team dependencies. AI enhances their ability to stay aligned with strategic intent:

* **Predictive Scheduling**: AI analyzes historical project data to forecast risks in delivery timelines.
* Dependency Tracking: Algorithms map dependencies across projects, making sure one team’s delays don’t derail strategic goals.
* Outcome-Based Reporting: Instead of measuring success by outputs delivered, AI helps PMs track whether outcomes align with organizational vision.

This shift from output-driven reporting to outcome-driven tracking is what keeps projects from becoming “busy work.” If you’re a PM wanting to master this shift, [AI for Project Managers Certification Training](../artificial-intelligence/ai-for-project-managers-certification-training) is built exactly for that need.

---

## Product Owners: Translating Vision Into Backlogs With AI

Product Owners hold the critical responsibility of breaking down strategy into practical product increments. Here’s how AI supports them:

* **Backlog Prioritization**: AI evaluates customer behavior, usage patterns, and market data to rank features that align with the vision.
* Customer-Centric Validation: AI-driven A/B testing shows whether a backlog item actually serves the customer and aligns with business goals.
* Roadmap Evolution: Instead of static roadmaps, AI helps Product Owners create adaptive ones that evolve with market feedback.

This is where [AI for Product Owners Certification Training](../artificial-intelligence/ai-for-product-owners-certification-training) becomes vital, it shows how AI tools help translate leadership vision into product roadmaps that deliver measurable impact.

---

## Scrum Masters: Guarding Execution Alignment With AI

Scrum Masters are guardians of team agility and delivery. AI enhances their role by ensuring teams don’t just deliver but deliver in alignment with vision:

* **Team Performance Insights**: AI tools track team velocity, predict burnout risks, and suggest corrective actions.
* Facilitating Feedback Loops: AI can summarize sprint reviews and retro data, surfacing patterns that may otherwise be overlooked.
* Alignment Checkpoints: AI ensures that what teams deliver is consistently tied back to objectives, reducing the risk of misaligned sprints.

Scrum Masters who upskill with [AI for Scrum Masters Training](../artificial-intelligence/ai-for-scrum-masters-training) learn how to integrate these AI capabilities into daily Agile practices.

---

## AI in Action: Practical Scenarios of Vision-to-Execution Alignment

To make this concrete, let’s look at some scenarios where AI strengthens alignment:

1. **OKR Tracking**  
    AI can track Objectives and Key Results across multiple departments, automatically flagging when execution drifts away from the vision.
2. Resource Allocation  
    AI reallocates resources dynamically based on evolving priorities. If one strategic initiative needs more capacity, AI helps rebalance work without derailing other projects.
3. Customer Feedback Loops  
    AI mines customer reviews and social media to detect shifts in sentiment. Leadership gets real-time insights into whether execution is creating the intended customer impact.
4. Portfolio-Level Alignment  
    Tools like enterprise AI platforms aggregate progress across portfolios, making it clear whether the sum of all projects truly supports the vision.

For deeper reading on these applications, check out [Harvard Business Review’s perspective on AI and strategic execution](https://hbr.org/2023/03/how-to-ensure-your-ai-initiatives-deliver-on-their-promise).

---

## The Human-AI Partnership: Why Both Matter

It’s easy to assume AI alone can ensure alignment, but the truth is alignment is as much about culture and leadership as it is about technology. AI surfaces the data, insights, and patterns, but humans make the final calls and drive the emotional alignment teams need.

Think of AI as the navigation system in a car. It shows the best route, alerts you to traffic, and recalculates when needed, but the driver still decides how to steer and when to stop.

---

## Building AI Competence Across Roles

To really strengthen alignment, organizations need role-specific AI skills:

* **Leaders**: Strategic adoption of AI for decision-making and cultural alignment.
* Project Managers: AI for planning, monitoring, and cross-project alignment.
* Product Owners: AI for backlog management, customer insights, and roadmap planning.
* Scrum Masters: AI for team health, sprint alignment, and continuous improvement.

This is why specialized certifications like [AI for Agile Leaders & Change Agents](../artificial-intelligence/ai-for-agile-leaders-change-agents-certification), [AI for Project Managers](../artificial-intelligence/ai-for-project-managers-certification-training), [AI for Product Owners](../artificial-intelligence/ai-for-product-owners-certification-training), and [AI for Scrum Masters](../artificial-intelligence/ai-for-scrum-masters-training) are critical. They provide structured learning tailored to how each role contributes to aligning vision with execution.

---

## Final Thoughts

Alignment from vision to execution has always been the foundation of successful organizations. AI doesn’t replace the need for strong leadership, clear communication, and enabled teams, but it does remove blind spots, reduce misalignment, and accelerate feedback loops.

What this really means is that organizations that embrace AI not just for automation but for alignment will execute strategies faster, with fewer missteps, and with more measurable impact.

The journey from vision to execution is no longer a leap of faith. With AI, it becomes a guided, data-informed path where leaders and teams move together toward a shared future.

### Balancing value, feasibility, and risk

## Analyst perspective

### Embed AI with discipline, clarity, and human oversight.

![](https://cdn1-public.infotech.com/blueprints/Select-and-Prioritize-AI-Use-Cases-for-Your-Law-Firm/kassim-dossa.jpg)

Law firms are under increasing pressure to engage with AI as client expectations, competitive dynamics, and internal cost structures continue to evolve. While interest in AI adoption is widespread, progress remains uneven, shaped by the profession’s heightened sensitivity to risk, confidentiality, and accountability. Traditional law firm economics, rooted in utilization, pyramid firm structures, and billable time, create tension when AI promises efficiency without a clear mechanism for recognizing return on investment.

Concerns around output accuracy, explainability, data privacy, and regulatory exposure raise the cost of error and slow adoption. These risks often translate into verification overhead, governance friction, and cautious deployment, particularly when initiatives are not well aligned to legal workflows or firm capabilities. AI investment decisions are further complicated by feasibility factors beyond technical performance, including data quality, workflow suitability, and uneven adoption readiness across practices. At the same time, firms must navigate a rapidly expanding legal AI market, where overlapping tools, uneven maturity, and evolving vendor roadmaps make it difficult to place durable investment bets.

Importantly, AI use cases carry implications beyond efficiency alone. Decisions about where and how AI is applied increasingly influence talent attraction and retention, professional development pathways, client perception, and market differentiation. As a result, selecting and prioritizing AI use cases in law firms is less about generating ideas and more about balancing strategic value, feasibility, and professional risk in an evolving market.

**Kassim Dossa, MBA**  
 Research Director  
 Info-Tech Research Group

The key barriers to success include:   * Concerns regarding the accuracy and reliability of AI model outputs. * Vendor-led education shapes how firms understand AI, resulting in tool-driven use case selection rather than workflow-driven, strategic prioritization. * Cultural resistance and inconsistent AI literacy weaken internal confidence in AI initiatives and willingness to explore more complex use cases. * Inherent difficulties in proving ROI driven by output verification costs and unclear efficiency gains. | Info-Tech’s human-centric, value-based approach is a guide for selecting and prioritizing AI use cases:   * Leverage a law-firm-specific business reference architecture to identify organization-aligned AI use cases and key metrics you want to improve. * Evaluate the firm’s AI maturity as part of the use case feasibility evaluation process. * Conduct a market feasibility scan to determine which use cases are supported by current AI capabilities. * Select and prioritize AI-based use cases across industry value drivers while understanding the execution implications. * Layer in governance structures to create conditions for success. |

**Info-Tech Insight**

Firms struggle to select and prioritize AI use cases as they lack clarity on the metrics they want to impact and underestimate the cultural resistance to change in how value is delivered.

## Your challenge

* Develop a business-capability-driven AI strategy that strengthens firm performance while minimizing investment, professional, and compliance risk.
* Placing risk-adjusted bets on AI tools that align with use cases, firm strategy, and AI maturity while balancing feasibility, ethical, and evolving regulatory constraints.
* Navigate the cost and security constraints of AI solutions while ensuring alignment with governance, privacy rules, and risk management standards.
* Uncover sustainable AI solutions in a rapidly shifting marketplace while resisting a tool-first approach to strategy.
* Address the need to upskill lawyers and staff to optimize productivity and resource allocation while delivering high quality outcomes and protecting client trust.
* Capture the competitive upside of AI implementation across talent, client acquisition, and brand differentiation while safeguarding the firm from avoidable risk.

## Law Firm Business Capability Map

### Business capability map defined

In business architecture, the primary view of an organization is known as a business capability map.

A business capability defines what a business does to enable value creation, rather than how. Business capabilities:

* Represent stable business functions.
* Are unique and independent of each other.
* Typically, they will have defined business outcomes.

A business capability map provides details that help the business architecture practitioner direct attention to a specific area of the business for further assessment.

## 1.1 Map your candidate AI use cases

d49.title: Pushpay Unveils New Strategic Partnerships and Integrations
d49.snippet:
Title: Pushpay Unveils New Strategic Partnerships and Integrations
# Pushpay Unveils New Strategic Partnerships and Integrations to Support Church Growth and Engagement. *New product integrations with* *Mailchimp* *and* *StudioC**, and a partnership with* *VisitorReach**, help ministries improve communication, outreach and foster deeper discipleship*. REDMOND, Wash., May 14, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Pushpay, the leading payments and engagement solutions provider for mission-driven organizations, today announces three new strategic partnerships and product integrations designed to further equip churches in their mission to build community and deepen connections for a greater Kingdom impact. Pushpay’s new partnership with **VisitorReach** enables churches to connect with their congregation more effortlessly through **VisitorTap**—a tap-to-engage technology designed specifically for churches. “We’re proud to expand our integration ecosystem, which is a part of a broader strategy to equip and empower ministry leaders with the tools they need to lead in a digitally connected world,” said Gruia Pitigoi-Aron, Pushpay’s Chief Product Officer. “Investing in a robust partnership and integration network helps our customers remove technology barriers, allowing them to focus more time on what matters most: their people.”. According to the company’s **2025 State of Church Technology** report, 86% of church leaders agree technology helps strengthen connection in their community. Several of the company’s new integrations are designed to help solve that challenge:. Saved Searches, Groups, and Process Queues within Pushpay’s ChMS can now be synced to Mailchimp tags or audiences, allowing churches to send more personalized and timely communications. * **StudioC Integration:** Pushpay’s enhanced mobile app experience now includes integration with StudioC, a technology company that helps churches strengthen discipleship and engagement through data-driven communication. The new mobile app integration helps churches guide people more intuitively through their spiritual journey by providing relevant content and next steps—helping churches deliver the right content, to the right people, at the right time. With over 80 integrations, Pushpay integrates with the majority of the top software solutions used by churches today, delivering a comprehensive and connected technology ecosystem for its more than 15,000 customers. For more information about today’s announcement, or Pushpay’s growing integration ecosystem, visit www.pushpay.com/integrations. Pushpay Invests in the Future of Faith with Launch of Pushpay Goes Technology Grant for Church Planters.

d54.title: AI ile Dijital Kampanyalarda Hedef Kitle Segmentasyonu
d54.snippet: AI sayesinde yaş, cinsiyet, lokasyon gibi demografik veriler otomatik olarak analiz edilip segmentlere dönüştürülebiliyor. Bu sayede klasik
d54.content:
AI ile Dijital Kampanyalarda Hedef Kitle Segmentasyonu
Dijital pazarlama kampanyalarının başarısı artık yalnızca kreatif fikirlerle değil, doğru kişilere ulaşmakla ölçülüyor. Hedef kitleye ulaşamayan kampanyalar, ne kadar yaratıcı olursa olsun başarıya ulaşamıyor. Bu noktada hedef kitle segmentasyonu, pazarlamanın temel taşı haline geliyor.
Geleneksel segmentasyon yöntemleri artık yeterli değil. Veriye dayalı karar alma süreçlerinin ön planda olduğu bu çağda, yapay zeka destekli segmentasyon sistemleri markaların rekabette öne çıkmasını sağlıyor. AI, büyük veri kümeleri üzerinde milisaniyelerle çalışan algoritmalarıyla daha doğru, daha derin ve daha hızlı hedefleme yapmayı mümkün kılıyor.
Hedef Kitle Segmentasyonu Nedir, Neden Önemlidir?
Segmentasyon, kitlenizi belirli özelliklerine göre alt gruplara ayırarak onlara özel pazarlama mesajları oluşturmanızı sağlar. Doğru segmentasyon, kampanyaların dönüşüm oranlarını artırır, reklam bütçesini daha verimli hale getirir ve kullanıcı deneyimini kişiselleştirir.
Geleneksel olarak bu segmentasyon; yaş, cinsiyet, lokasyon gibi sınırlı verilerle yapılırken, AI artık davranışsal verileri, satın alma geçmişlerini, hatta duygusal tonlamaları bile analiz edebiliyor. Bu da pazarlamacıların tahmine değil veriye dayalı kararlar almasını sağlıyor.
AI’nin segmentasyon süreçlerine getirdiği hız ve doğruluk
Yapay zeka, büyük hacimli verileri analiz ederek hedef kitleyi birkaç saniye içinde mikro-segmentlere ayırabiliyor. Bu sayede manuel analiz süreçlerine kıyasla hem zaman hem doğruluk açısından büyük bir avantaj sağlanıyor.
AI ile Segmentasyon Türleri
Yapay zeka, farklı türde segmentasyon modelleriyle pazarlamacıların daha spesifik hedef kitleler oluşturmasına olanak tanır. Her segmentasyon türü, farklı kampanya amaçlarına hizmet eder ve hedef kitlenin ihtiyaçlarına daha doğru cevap verilmesini sağlar.
AI destekli segmentasyon modelleri, klasik demografik analizleri bir adım öteye taşıyarak ilgi alanı, davranışsal örüntüler, zamanlama ve tahmini satın alma eğilimlerine göre gruplamalar yapar. Bu da çok daha etkili kampanya yapıları oluşturulmasını sağlar.
Demografik Segmentasyon
AI sayesinde yaş, cinsiyet, lokasyon gibi demografik veriler otomatik olarak analiz edilip segmentlere dönüştürülebiliyor. Bu sayede klasik hedefleme yöntemleri daha hızlı ve verimli hale geliyor.
İlgi alanı ve davranış temelli segmentasyon
Kullanıcıların web sitesi veya uygulamadaki etkileşimleri üzerinden ilgi alanları ve davranış örüntüleri belirlenerek dinamik segmentler oluşturulabiliyor. Bu model, ürün önerileri ve içerik sunumlarında yüksek oranda kişiselleştirme sağlar.
Alışveriş döngüsüne göre segmentasyon (AI tahmini ile)
AI, kullanıcının hangi aşamada olduğunu (ilk ziyaret, ürün inceleme, sepete ekleme, terk etme) analiz ederek hedeflemeyi buna göre şekillendirebilir. Bu da daha isabetli reklam gösterimlerini ve zamanında müdahale fırsatlarını doğurur.
Segmentasyon için AI’dan Yararlanılan Veri Kaynakları
Yapay zekanın etkili şekilde çalışabilmesi için doğru ve kapsamlı veri kaynaklarına ihtiyaç vardır. Segmentasyon stratejileri, yalnızca analitik araçlardan gelen verilerle değil; CRM, sosyal medya, web davranışları ve üçüncü parti veri kaynaklarıyla da zenginleştirilebilir.
Bu veri kaynaklarının entegrasyonu sayesinde AI, çok daha gelişmiş bir bağlamda kullanıcı analizi yapar. Özellikle davranışsal ve etkileşimsel verilerin işlenmesiyle kullanıcıların gelecekteki davranışlarını öngören modeller kurmak mümkün hale gelir.
LinkedIn tarafından öneriliyor
AI Modelleriyle Segmentasyon Nasıl Kurulur?
Segmentasyonun yapay zeka ile yapılabilmesi için, öncelikle hangi modelin kullanılacağına ve hangi verilerin işleneceğine karar verilmesi gerekir. AI modelleri, veriyi öğrenen ve gelişen algoritmalar sayesinde geleneksel filtreleme yöntemlerinden daha güçlü segmentasyonlar üretir.
Bu süreçte hem dil tabanlı modeller (LLM’ler) hem de sayısal modeller (makine öğrenmesi) birlikte kullanılabilir. Böylece hem davranışsal içgörüler hem de skor bazlı değerleme sistemleri oluşturmak mümkün olur.
GPT tabanlı promptlarla müşteri profili çıkarma
LLM modelleriyle müşteri e-postaları, destek talepleri ve sosyal medya yorumları gibi metin tabanlı veriler analiz edilerek, kullanıcıların ihtiyaçları ve kişilik profilleri hakkında detaylı çıkarımlar yapılabilir.
LLM ve makine öğrenmesi ile müşteri kümelenmesi (clustering)
Kullanıcıların benzer davranış ve alışkanlıklarına göre gruplanması, özellikle pazarlama otomasyon sistemleri için oldukça kritik bir rol oynar. AI ile oluşturulan bu kümeler, özelleştirilmiş pazarlama akışlarının temelini oluşturur.
K-Means, RFM analizi ve AI destekli müşteri puanlaması
Segmentasyonun nicel tarafında RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) analizleri K-Means algoritmasıyla desteklenerek müşterilere puanlama yapılabilir. Bu sayede hangi müşteriye ne zaman ve ne sunulacağı önceden belirlenebilir.
Kurumsal Kampanya Türlerine Göre Segmentasyon Stratejileri
Kurumsal kampanyalar farklı amaçlara yönelik olarak tasarlanır: yeni müşteri kazanımı, sadakat artırımı, terk eden müşterilerin geri kazanılması gibi. Her bir kampanya türü, kendine özgü segmentasyon stratejisi gerektirir.
AI burada devreye girerek, hangi kampanya türü için hangi kullanıcı grubunun en uygun olduğunu otomatik olarak tespit edebilir. Böylece pazarlama ekipleri stratejilerini daha hızlı ve etkili bir şekilde uygulayabilir.
Yeni müşteri kazanım kampanyaları için hedefleme
AI, potansiyel müşteri adaylarını analiz ederek “satın almaya yakınlık skoru” gibi metrikler oluşturabilir. Bu da yeni kullanıcıları kazanmak için daha yüksek dönüşüm sağlayacak hedeflemeleri mümkün kılar.
Gerçek Hayattan Kurumsal Uygulama Örnekleri
Yapay zeka tabanlı segmentasyon, yalnızca teoride değil pratikte de birçok başarı hikayesine imza atmıştır. Özellikle lokasyon ve davranış farklarının analiz edilmesi, büyük ölçekli kampanyalarda fark yaratmaktadır.
Örnek: Türkiye genelinde hizmet veren bir e-ticaret firması, farklı şehirlerdeki kullanıcıların hafta içi ve hafta sonu alışveriş davranışlarını analiz ederek kampanyalarını bölgesel olarak özelleştirdi. Bu hiper-bölgesel segmentasyon, %27 daha fazla dönüşüm oranı elde edilmesini sağladı.
Geleceğin Segmentasyonu: Hiper-Kişiselleştirme Dönemi
Gelecekte segmentasyonun sınırları ortadan kalkacak. Her kullanıcı, kendi segmenti olacak. AI, her bireye özel teklifler ve deneyimler sunarak pazarlamayı “kitlesel kişiselleştirme” seviyesinden “kişisel deneyim yönetimi” seviyesine taşıyacak.
Hiper-kişiselleştirme dönemi, yalnızca pazarlama ekiplerinin değil; CRM, ürün geliştirme ve satış ekiplerinin de AI ile daha entegre çalışmasını gerektirecek. Bu dönüşüm, rekabet avantajı kazanmak isteyen markalar için artık bir seçenek değil, zorunluluk.

# Gizlilik Politikası

Son güncelleme: 16.07.2026

## 1. Giriş, Amaç ve Kapsam

Apilex ("Şirket", "biz"), hukuk profesyonelleri için yapay zek destekli hukuk araştırma, içtihat analizi ve belge üretim hizmetleri sunan bir teknoloji şirketidir. Bu Gizlilik Politikası ("Politika") ile, 6698 sayılı Kişisel Verilerin Korunması Kanunu ("KVKK") uyarınca; [www.apilex.ai](https://www.apilex.ai) internet sitemiz ve Apilex platformumuz (topluca "Hizmetlerimiz") aracılığıyla kişisel verilerinizi nasıl ve hangi sebeplere dayanarak topladığımızı, sakladığımızı, kullandığımızı, paylaştığımızı ve başka şekillerde işlediğimizi açıklamaktayız.

Kişisel verilerinizin bu Politika'da açıklandığı şekilde işlenmesi hakkında sorularınız olması halinde, lütfen aşağıda yer alan "Veri Sorumlusu Kimliği ve İletişim Bilgileri" bölümündeki iletişim bilgilerinden bize ulaşınız.

## 2. Veri Sorumlusu Kimliği ve İletişim Bilgileri

Kişisel verileriniz, KVKK uyarınca veri sorumlusu sıfatıyla aşağıda unvanı belirtilen şirket ("Apilex", "Şirket", "biz") tarafından işlenmektedir:

* **Unvan:** APİLEX TEKNOLOJİ ANONİM ŞİRKETİ
* **Adres:** Osmangazi Mah. 3117. Sokak Altınbaş Teknopark No:3/15 Esenyurt/İstanbul
* **E-posta:** [privacy@apilex.ai](mailto:privacy@apilex.ai)
* **KEP:** [apilexteknoloji@hs01.kep.tr](mailto:apilexteknoloji@hs01.kep.tr)

## 3. Bu Politikanın Diğer Aydınlatma Metinleriyle İlişkisi

Bu Politika, Apilex'in kişisel veri işleme faaliyetlerine ilişkin genel çerçeveyi ve temel ilkeleri düzenleyen çatı bir belge niteliğindedir. İnternet Sitesi ziyaretçilerine, iletişim formu/demo talebi/destek talebi süreçlerine, kariyer başvurularına ve çalışanlarımıza, çalışan adaylarına, stajyerlerimize ve tedarikçi çalışanlarına ilişkin süreçler dahil olmak üzere, kişisel veri işlediğimiz her bir sürece özgü olarak KVKK'nın 10. maddesi uyarınca ayrıca aydınlatma metinleri yayımlanır; söz konusu aydınlatma metinleri işbu Politika ile birlikte ve işbu Politika'da yer alan temel ilkelerle uyumlu olarak yorumlanır. Aydınlatma metinleri ile işbu Politika arasında bir çelişki bulunması hlinde, ilgili sürece özgü aydınlatma metni esas alınır.

Şirket çalışanlarına, çalışan adaylarına, stajyerlerine ve tedarikçi çalışanlarına ilişkin kişisel veri işleme faaliyetleri, işbu Politika'nın 4. ve devamı maddelerinde düzenlenen veri kategorileri, işleme amaçları ve saklama süreleri kapsamında değildir; bu kişiler için yukarıda belirtilen ayrı aydınlatma metinlerinde düzenlenen esaslar uygulanır.

Çerezlerin kullanımına ilişkin ayrıntılı bilgi için ayrıca yayımlanan [Çerez Politikası](/tr/cerez-politikasi) geçerlidir.

## 4. Toplanan Kişisel Veri Kategorileri

Kişisel verileriniz; internet sitemiz, platform arayüzümüz, çerezler ve benzer teknolojiler, destek ve iletişim formları ile e-posta kanalları aracılığıyla, tamamen veya kısmen otomatik yollarla ya da bir veri kayıt sisteminin parçası olmak kaydıyla otomatik olmayan yöntemlerle toplanmaktadır.

* **Kimlik Bilgisi:** Ad, soyad; faturalama gerektiren hllerde T.C. kimlik veya vergi numarası.
* **İletişim Bilgisi:** E-posta adresi, cep telefonu numarası.
* **Müşteri Ticari İşlem Bilgisi:** Abonelik ve paket bilgileri, fatura bilgileri, talep bilgileri, ücretsiz kullanım kodu, çağrı merkezi kayıtları.
* **Talep/Şikyet Bilgisi:** Demo talebi, iletişim formu mesajı veya destek talebi içeriği ile talebin tarih ve saati.
* **Kullanıcı Hesap Bilgisi:** Dil tercihiniz ve hesap ayarlarınız.
* **İçerik ve Hukuki Veriler:** Platforma yüklediğiniz belgeler ve bu belgelerde yer alan kişisel veriler; oluşturduğunuz özet, tablo ve taslaklar; Asistan'a girdiğiniz istemler (prompt'lar); arama geçmişiniz; projeleriniz.
* **Kullanım ve Teknik Veri:** Cihaz tanımlayıcı, IP adresi, tarayıcı ve işletim sistemi bilgisi, gezinme geçmişi, IP adresiyle ilişkilendirilebilecek yaklaşık konum bilgisi. Hizmetlerimizi kullanımınız sırasında, çerezler ve benzer teknolojiler aracılığıyla toplanır.

İçerik ve Hukuki Veriler kategorisi dışındaki yukarıdaki kişisel veri kategorileri, belirtilen amaçların gerçekleştirilmesiyle sınırlı ve bu amaçlar için gerekli olan ölçüde toplanır; amaçla bağlantısız veya ölçüsüz veri toplanmaz. İçerik ve Hukuki Veriler ise, bu veriler bakımından veri sorumlusu sıfatını taşıyan sizin kendi yükümlülüklerinizi yerine getirebilmenizi desteklemek amacıyla, sıfır veri saklama ilkesi çerçevesinde ele alınır.

Tarafların Rolleri: Veri Sorumlusu ve Veri İşleyen

Apilex; Kimlik, İletişim, Müşteri İşlem, Talep/Şikyet, Kullanıcı Hesap ve Kullanım/Teknik Veri kategorileri bakımından veri sorumlusudur.

İçerik ve Hukuki Veriler farklıdır. Bunlar sizin platforma yüklediğiniz dava dosyaları, sözleşmeler ve bu belgelerdeki üçüncü kişilere (müvekkiliniz, karşı taraf, tanık vb.) ait kişisel verilerdir. Bu veriler bakımından veri sorumlusu sizsiniz; Apilex ise yalnızca sizin talimatlarınızla hareket eden veri işleyendir. Bu nedenle, yüklediğiniz belgelerdeki üçüncü kişilere ait verilerin hukuka uygun şekilde elde edilmiş olmasından, bu kişilerin gerektiğinde aydınlatılmasından ve işlemenin uygun bir hukuki sebebe dayanmasından siz sorumlusunuz.

Platform sıfır veri saklama politikası ile operasyonlarını yürütür. Bu prensibe bağlı olarak; teknik süreçlerinde teknoloji iş ortaklarıyla da bağlayıcı hizmet anlaşmaları ile kullanıcı verilerini, yapay zeka modeline gönderilen komut ve sorguları modelin ürettiği yanıtları, hiçbir şekilde sunucuda saklamaz. KVKK, GDPR yükümlülüklerine uyumlu şekilde, platformda işlem çağrısı bittiği anda veriler tamamen silinir. Platformda yer alan veya gelecekte yer alacak modeli eğitmek ve geliştirmek için kullanılmaz. İçerikleriniz şifrelenerek saklanır ve yalnızca yetkilendirilmiş personelimiz tarafından, destek talebiniz veya teknik sorun giderme gibi sınırlı amaçlarla erişilebilir.

Hizmetlerimiz kapsamında ürettiğimiz yapay zek destekli çıktılar (dilekçe taslakları, sözleşme taslakları, özetler, analizler vb.) yalnızca birer taslak ve referans materyalidir; hukuki danışmanlık niteliği taşımaz ve hakkınızda veya üçüncü kişiler hakkında münhasıran otomatik sistemler tarafından verilen, sizi bağlayıcı bir karar oluşturmaz. Bu çıktıların doğruluğunu ve somut olaya uygunluğunu teyit etmek, kullanılmadan önce bir hukuk profesyoneline danışmak sizin sorumluluğunuzdadır.

Hizmetlerimiz kapsamında kullanıcı davranışlarınıza ilişkin bir profilleme yapılmaz.

Özel Nitelikli Kişisel Verilerin İşlenmesi

Platforma yüklediğiniz hukuki belgeler (dava dosyaları, sözleşmeler vb.), istisnai olarak sağlık verisi, ceza mahkûmiyeti ve güvenlik tedbirlerine ilişkin veri, sendika üyeliği gibi özel nitelikli kişisel veriler içerebilir. Bu veriler bakımından da veri sorumlusu sizsiniz; Apilex bu verileri yalnızca sizin talimatlarınız doğrultusunda, veri işleyen sıfatıyla işler. Bu verilerin hukuka uygun şekilde işlenmesini sağlamak sizin sorumluluğunuzdadır.

## 5. Kişisel Verilerin İşlenme Amaçları ve Hukuki Sebepleri

* **Hesabınızın oluşturulması, sözleşme ilişkimizin kurulması ve yürütülmesi ile sizinle iletişime geçilmesi:** sözleşmenin kurulması veya ifasıyla doğrudan doğruya ilgili olması hukuki sebebine dayanarak.
* **Satış, satış sonrası destek, üretim ve operasyon ile müşteri ilişkileri yönetimi süreçlerinin yürütülmesi:** sözleşmenin kurulması veya ifasıyla doğrudan doğruya ilgili olması hukuki sebebine dayanarak.
* **Hizmetlerimizin sunulması, geliştirilmesi ve size özel hle getirilmesi:** sözleşmenin kurulması veya ifasıyla doğrudan doğruya ilgili olması hukuki sebebine dayanarak.
* **Demo talebinizin değerlendirilmesi için sizinle iletişime geçilmesi:** sözleşmenin kurulmasından önce gerekli olan tedbirlerin alınması hukuki sebebine dayanarak.
* **İletişim formu ile ilettiğiniz mesajın değerlendirilmesi ve size geri dönüş yapılması:** temel hak ve özgürlüklerinize zarar vermemek kaydıyla meşru menfaatimiz hukuki sebebine dayanarak.
* **Destek talebinizin karşılanması:** üye iseniz sözleşmenin ifasıyla doğrudan doğruya ilgili olması, üye değilseniz meşru menfaatimiz hukuki sebebine dayanarak.
* Ürün ve hizmetlerimizle ilgili sizinle iletişimde kalmak ve pazarlama analizi çalışmaları yürütmek amacıyla iletişim bilgileriniz, temel hak ve özgürlüklerinize zarar vermemek kaydıyla meşru menfaatimiz hukuki sebebine dayanarak işlenebilir. Ancak size ticari elektronik ileti (e-posta/SMS ile tanıtım, kampanya, promosyon vb.) gönderebilmemiz için, 6563 sayılı Elektronik Ticaretin Düzenlenmesi Hakkında Kanun ve İleti Yönetim Sistemi (İYS) uyarınca ayrıca açık rızanızı alırız; bu rızayı dilediğiniz zaman geri çekebilirsiniz.
* **Hizmetlerimizin güvenliğinin sağlanması, hatalı kullanımların tespit edilmesi ve Hizmetlerimizin geliştirilmesi:** meşru menfaatimiz hukuki sebebine dayanarak.
* **Hukuki yükümlülüklerimizin yerine getirilmesi ve yetkili mercilere bilgi verilmesi:** kanunlarda açıkça öngörülmüş olması hukuki sebebine dayanarak.

Meşru menfaatimize dayandığımız hllerde, önce bu menfaatin gerçekten var olduğunu, ardından bu menfaatin temel hak ve özgürlüklerinizi zedelemediğini değerlendiren iki aşamalı bir denge testi uygularız.

## 6. Kişisel Verilerin Aktarılması

Kişisel verileriniz aşağıdaki alıcı gruplarına aktarılabilir:

Yurt içinde:

* **Ödeme kuruluşumuz:** ödeme ve tahsilat işlemlerinin gerçekleştirilmesi amacıyla.
* **Web analitik ve reklam hizmeti sağlayıcımız:** internet sitemizin ve Hizmetlerimizin kullanımının analiz edilmesi ile pazarlama faaliyetlerinin yürütülmesi amacıyla.
* **Yetkili kamu kurum ve kuruluşları:** hukuki yükümlülüklerimizin yerine getirilmesi ve yetkili mercilere bilgi verilmesi amacıyla.

Yurt dışında:

* **Barındırma (hosting) hizmeti sağlayıcımız:** Hizmetlerimizin barındırılması ve verilerinizin güvenli şekilde depolanması amacıyla.
* **Yapay zek destekli analiz ve içerik üretimi hizmeti sağlayıcılarımız:** platform üzerinden talep ettiğiniz yapay zek destekli araştırma, analiz ve belge üretimi işlevlerinin sağlanması amacıyla.
* **Ödeme kuruluşumuz:** ödeme ve tahsilat işlemlerinin gerçekleştirilmesi amacıyla.
* **Web analitik ve reklam hizmeti sağlayıcımız:** internet sitemizin ve Hizmetlerimizin kullanımının analiz edilmesi ile pazarlama faaliyetlerinin yürütülmesi amacıyla.
* **Yetkili kamu kurum ve kuruluşları:** hukuki yükümlülüklerimizin yerine getirilmesi amacıyla.

Yeterlilik kararı bulunmayan ülkelere yaptığımız aktarımlar, KVKK m.9 kapsamında öngörülen uygun güvence mekanizmaları çerçevesinde gerçekleştirilir.

## 7. Kişisel Verilerin Saklanma Süresi ve İmhası

Kişisel verileriniz, ilgili mevzuatta öngörülen veya işlendikleri amaç için gerekli olan süre kadar saklanır. Buna göre:

* **Üyelik, satış ve sipariş süreçlerine ilişkin kayıtlarınız:** sözleşme ilişkisinin sona ermesini takiben 10 yıl süreyle saklanır.
* **Pazarlama faaliyetleri kapsamında işlenen verileriniz:** ilgili faaliyetin sona ermesinden itibaren 5 yıl süreyle saklanır.
* **Demo talebi, iletişim formu ve destek talebi kapsamındaki işlem kayıtlarınız:** talebinizin sonuçlandırılmasından itibaren 1 yıl süreyle saklanır.
* **İçerik ve Hukuki Verileriniz (yüklediğiniz belgeler, istemleriniz, arama geçmişiniz, projeleriniz):** hesabınızı sildiğinizde derhal ve kalıcı olarak silinir; hesabınızı silmemeniz hlinde bu verilere ilişkin loglar 1 yıl süreyle saklanır.
* **Kullanım ve Teknik Verileriniz:** 1 yıl süreyle saklanır.
* **Bilgi güvenliği amacıyla tutulan günlük (log) kayıtlarınız:** 5 yıl süreyle saklanır.

Saklama süresinin sonunda kişisel verileriniz, Kişisel Veri Saklama ve İmha Politikamızda belirtilen usullere göre re'sen veya talebiniz üzerine silinir; elektronik ortamda güvenli silme yöntemleriyle, fiziksel ortamda ise geri döndürülemeyecek şekilde yok edilir. Bazı hllerde veriler, maskeleme veya toplulaştırma gibi tekniklerle anonim hle getirilerek istatistiksel amaçlarla saklanmaya devam edebilir.

## 8. Çerezler

Hizmetlerimiz kapsamında, Site'nin çalışmasını sağlamak, kullanımı analiz etmek ve deneyiminizi iyileştirmek amacıyla çerezler ve benzer teknolojiler kullanılmaktadır. Zorunlu çerezler dışındaki çerezler (analiz, işlevsellik, reklam/hedefleme gibi) için açık rızanız alınır; bu rızayı çerez tercih paneli üzerinden istediğiniz zaman geri çekebilir veya değiştirebilirsiniz. Çerez türleri, kullanım amaçları, saklama süreleri ve tercihlerinizi nasıl yönetebileceğinize ilişkin ayrıntılı bilgiye [Çerez Politikası](/tr/cerez-politikasi)'ndan ulaşabilirsiniz.

## 9. Kişisel Verilerinizin Güvenliğine İlişkin Alınan Tedbirler

Kişisel verilerinizin hukuka aykırı olarak işlenmesini ve bu verilere yetkisiz erişimi önlemek amacıyla; erişim yetki matrisi ve kontrolü, günlük (log) kayıtlarının düzenli tutulması ve incelenmesi, şifreleme, güvenlik duvarları, düzenli sızma testleri ve zafiyet taramaları, veri kaybı önleme ve veri maskeleme uygulamaları, yedekleme ile saldırı tespit ve önleme sistemleri dahil olmak üzere gerekli teknik tedbirleri; kişisel veri işleme envanterinin güncel tutulması, çalışan gizlilik taahhütnameleri, düzenli farkındalık eğitimleri ve tedarikçi/veri işleyen denetimi dahil olmak üzere gerekli idari tedbirleri almaktayız. Bilgi güvenliği süreçlerimiz, uluslararası standartlarla (ISO 27001) uyumlu şekilde yürütülmektedir.

Bir veri ihlali meydana gelmesi hlinde, durumu gecikmeksizin ve en geç 72 saat içinde Kişisel Verileri Koruma Kurulu'na ve etkilenen ilgili kişilere bildiririz.

## 10. Kişisel Verileriniz Üzerindeki Kontrolünüz

Hesap bilgilerinizi ve gizlilik tercihlerinizi [Ayarlar sayfası](https://app.apilex.ai/settings) üzerinden görüntüleyebilir ve yönetebilirsiniz. Hesabınızı silmek istemeniz hlinde Ayarlar > Profil > Hesabı Sil adımlarını izleyerek doğrudan talepte bulunabilirsiniz.

## 11. İlgili Kişi Hakları ve Başvuru Usulü

KVKK'nın 11. maddesi uyarınca İlgili Kişi olarak aşağıdaki haklara sahipsiniz:

* Kişisel veri işlenip işlenmediğini öğrenme,
* Kişisel verileri işlenmişse buna ilişkin bilgi talep etme,
* Kişisel verilerin işlenme amacını ve amacına uygun kullanılıp kullanılmadığını öğrenme,
* Yurt içinde veya yurt dışında kişisel verilerin aktarıldığı üçüncü kişileri bilme,
* Kişisel verilerin eksik veya yanlış işlenmiş olması hlinde bunların düzeltilmesini isteme,
* Mevzuatta öngörülen şartlar çerçevesinde kişisel verilerin silinmesini veya yok edilmesini isteme,
* Yukarıdaki iki bent uyarınca yapılan işlemlerin, verilerin aktarıldığı üçüncü kişilere bildirilmesini isteme,
* İşlenen verilerin münhasıran otomatik sistemler vasıtasıyla analiz edilmesi suretiyle aleyhinize bir sonucun ortaya çıkmasına itiraz etme,
* Kişisel verilerin kanuna aykırı işlenmesi sebebiyle zarara uğramanız hlinde zararın giderilmesini talep etme.

Bu haklarınızı kullanmak için talebinizi, kimliğinizi tevsik edici belgelerle birlikte bize iletebilirsiniz. Bunun için Madde 2'de yer alan adresimize yazılı olarak, KEP adresimize, güvenli elektronik imza veya mobil imza ile ya da sistemimizde kayıtlı e-posta adresinizden [privacy@apilex.ai](mailto:privacy@apilex.ai) adresine başvurabilirsiniz. Başvurunuz, niteliğine göre en kısa sürede ve en geç otuz gün içinde ücretsiz olarak sonuçlandırılır; işlemin ayrıca bir maliyet gerektirmesi hlinde Kurulca belirlenen tarifedeki ücret alınabilir. Talebinizin reddedilmesi, yetersiz bulunması veya süresinde cevap verilmemesi hlinde, cevabı öğrendiğiniz tarihten itibaren otuz gün ve her hlde başvuru tarihinden itibaren altmış gün içinde Kişisel Verileri Koruma Kurulu'na şikyette bulunabilirsiniz.

## 12. Güncellemeler ve Yürürlük

Bu Politika'yı zaman zaman güncelleyebiliriz. Güncel sürüm bu sayfada yayımlanır. Esaslı değişiklikler yapılması hlinde, uygun iletişim kanalları aracılığıyla sizi bilgilendiririz. Bu Politika, yayımlandığı tarihten itibaren yürürlüğe girer.

d60.content: Best AI Automation Use Cases for Industrial B2B Industrial B2B companies are reimagining operations through artificial intelligence. What once required manual oversight - production planning, asset monitoring, quality checks, and inventory forecasting - can now run through automated systems guided by AI. Leading firms use it to predict maintenance needs, reduce waste, and keep global supply networks aligned. The result? Faster cycles, fewer disruptions, and more informed decisions. Quick Takeaways ●​ Predictive maintenance is the top AI automation case study in industrial B2B, cutting downtime and repair costs. ●​ AI-driven quality control boosts throughput and accuracy on production lines. ●​ Automated supply chain forecasting improves planning, visibility, and resilience. ●​ AI-assisted service automation enhances field efficiency and customer satisfaction. ●​ Long-term success requires data readiness and leadership alignment. Why Industrial B2B Needs AI Automation Industrial businesses rely on precision and reliability around the clock. But the growing complexity of supply chains, global markets, and connected assets has pushed manual systems past their limits. Every second of downtime, every unplanned delay, carries cost. AI automation gives industrial leaders the ability to operate proactively instead of reactively. Data from machines, sensors, and systems flows into models that predict failures, streamline logistics, and optimize performance. For B2B manufacturers, this amplifies expertise and creates a smarter ecosystem for decision-making. Firms that adopt AI automation effectively have an edge that compounds: less waste, more uptime, and a tighter link between strategy and execution. Image source Alt text: age of AI in business automation market graph Use Case #1: Predictive Maintenance and Asset Reliability Few AI automation case studies show as much value as predictive maintenance. Traditional maintenance runs on fixed schedules or failure responses. AI is the opposite. Machine learning models analyze vibration, temperature, and operational data from connected equipment to detect early signs of wear or failure. That information triggers service before a breakdown occurs. Key benefits include: ●​ Lower unplanned downtime through real-time alerts. ●​ Optimized maintenance cycles that extend asset life. ●​ Improved workforce allocation by reducing emergency repairs. ●​ Reduced spare part inventory through better forecasting. What makes predictive maintenance effective is its scalability - models continuously refine themselves as more data flows in. Use Case #2: Automated Quality Control In industrial production, precision is everything. Even minor errors can cascade into expensive recalls or waste. AI automation - especially computer vision - enables inspection systems to detect defects faster and more consistently than human operators. These systems use high-resolution imaging and machine learning to compare parts against defined standards. The result is faster throughput and greater consistency. Implementation steps include: ●​ Installing cameras or sensors at critical points of assembly. ●​ Training models with labeled examples of acceptable and defective parts. ●​ Integrating alerts with production dashboards for immediate response. ●​ Feeding inspection data back into product design to address root causes. AI-driven quality control has moved beyond experimental pilots. In many B2B manufacturing environments, it’s now central to efficiency, accuracy, and safety. Use Case #3: Supply Chain Optimization Industrial B2B companies rely on complex supply networks spanning continents. Variability in demand, transportation, or supplier reliability can disrupt production and erode margins. AI automation improves visibility and response. Automation tools now use machine learning to forecast demand, detect bottlenecks, and adjust procurement or logistics in real time. The result is a supply chain that can adapt to conditions without constant manual oversight. Core capabilities include: ●​ Predictive demand forecasting based on production and external data. ●​ Dynamic inventory management that adjusts stock levels automatically. ●​ Supplier performance analytics that flag potential risks early. ●​ Automated replenishment workflows triggered by data signals. Industrial leaders using AI-enabled supply chain systems report lower working capital requirements, faster delivery, and more stable customer relationships. Use Case #4: Service and Field Operations Automation Industrial service operations - whether maintaining turbines, HVAC systems, or production equipment - often struggle with scale. Technicians must manage large territories, and travel costs are high. AI automation helps service teams prioritize work orders, predict repair needs, and assist technicians remotely. Combined with IoT monitoring, service automation transforms reactive service models into predictive ones. Practical applications: ●​ Remote monitoring of assets to predict and prevent failures. ●​ AI-based scheduling to allocate technicians based on urgency and location. ●​ Guided troubleshooting using augmented reality or digital twins. ●​ Feedback loops where every service report trains future models. The result is faster resolution, reduced downtime, and improved customer retention - key outcomes for industrial B2B companies that depend on long-term service contracts. Use Case #5: Production Planning and Process Optimization AI automation also optimizes how industrial plants plan production. Machine learning models evaluate order patterns, equipment status, and material availability to recommend optimal production sequences. Instead of static schedules, plants run with dynamic plans that adapt to real conditions. Production lines stay balanced, bottlenecks are minimized, and throughput rises. Industrial B2B firms using AI-assisted planning have reported: ●​ Shorter cycle times. ●​ Higher resource utilization. ●​ Lower energy consumption. ●​ Better alignment between production and customer demand. Over time, automated planning systems evolve into strategic decision tools - supporting managers in forecasting output, pricing, and resource investments. Building the Foundation for AI Automation No matter the use case, success in AI automation depends on a few shared foundations. 1. Data Quality and Integration AI systems can only perform as well as the data they learn from. Industrial B2B firms must unify data across ERP, MES, and IoT systems. Inconsistent or siloed data can erode the accuracy of models. 2. Cloud and Edge Infrastructure Industrial environments generate large volumes of data that require scalable storage and computing power. Edge computing handles time-sensitive decisions near the source, while cloud systems manage aggregation and training. 3. Governance and Oversight Every automation system needs governance—clear ownership, transparency in model behavior, and compliance with safety and privacy standards. Human oversight remains essential, especially for decisions that affect safety or customer trust. 4. Change Management Automation succeeds when people understand it. Workers and managers must trust outputs and know how to act on insights. Training, communication, and clear processes make that possible. When these elements align, AI automation shifts from a single project to a long-term operational advantage. Measuring ROI on AI Automation For industrial leaders, automation must show measurable value. The right metrics connect operational improvements to financial performance. Key performance indicators include: ●​ Unplanned downtime reduction (%) ●​ Maintenance cost savings ●​ Defect rate decline ●​ Inventory turnover improvement ●​ Service resolution time ●​ Overall return on automation investment Tracking these metrics across business units reveals where AI automation has the greatest impact. Transparency in ROI also supports continued executive buy-in and resource allocation. What’s Next for Industrial AI Automation? As 2025 comes to a close, AI automation in industrial B2B is expanding beyond predictive analytics into autonomous decision-making. AI agents now handle repetitive coordination tasks - optimizing schedules, balancing energy use, and even recommending pricing strategies. We’ll also see deeper integration between AI automation and digital twins - virtual models of factories, machines, or systems that allow leaders to test scenarios before acting. The future isn’t just more data or faster machines. It’s a shift toward continuous intelligence - where every system learns, adapts, and improves automatically. Industrial firms that prepare now will lead not just in efficiency but in innovation. Video source What Should Industrial Leaders Do Next? Start with one automation domain where the data is clean and the value is clear, like predictive maintenance or quality control. Build cross-functional alignment between IT, operations, and business teams. Pilot, measure, and scale with governance in place. AI automation is more of an evolution than a quick win. d61.snippet: A FREYR virtual battery factory, for instance, provides 3D representations of the infrastructure, plant, machinery, equipment, human ergonomics, safety information, robots, automated guided vehicles, and detailed product and production simulations. [...] Siemens, for instance, used a wealth of production data to increase throughput of a production line of printed circuit boards by performing 30% fewer x-ray tests. They accomplished this task using AI to identify which boards were likely to benefit from inspection. The company collected large amounts of processes, parameters and other information about test results to feed the AI model as well as correlating 40,000 production parameters. [...] A digital twin of a BMW automotive factory is another example. With simulation, the entire planning phase of the manufacturing facility can happen in a virtual world, and everything can be tried out and tested. “The OEM knows with a high-level of confidence that a system is going to run and achieve the throughput on day one,” Andrews said.

[AI and Machine Learning](https://www.controleng.com/ai-and-machine-learning/)

# Four AI case study successes in industrial manufacturing

Manufacturers of all sizes are using artificial intelligence (AI) to produce more products faster, at lower cost and less risk.

![](https://www.controleng.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/CTL2401_WEB_IMG_A3_SoftRobotics_ChickenWings-Slider.jpeg)

Courtesy: A3, Soft Robotics

## **Artificial intelligence (AI) insights**

* Industrial AI revolutionizes manufacturing: AI trains robots for intricate tasks, utilizing synthetic data, doubling production throughput, predicting maintenance, and simulating virtual factories for optimal efficiency.
* AI-driven insights transform operations: Smart devices analyze 3D maps, alerting to anomalies, optimizing workflow, and enhancing quality control, ensuring timely interventions and continuous improvement in production lines.

---

Artificial intelligence (AI) is helping industrial manufacturers do more – from handling more types of materials and optimizing production lines to making timely maintenance interventions and even building smarter factories. Data from your factory can enable AI to optimize workflow—whether at a single production station or across a facility.

A pilot project is a good place to get started with AI. Experts at Invisible AI, NVIDIA and Siemens shared pertinent use cases of where industrial AI delivers value and makes factories smarter today.

## Using synthetic data to pick and place different objects with robots

AI makes it possible for robots to handle new types of materials, even raw poultry. With AI-based training, objects that were previously impossible for robots to identify and manipulate are now within their grasp.

An NVIDIA customer, Soft Robotics, for instance, worked with a food producer to create an AI solution that enables a robot to recognize and pick up single, wet and squishy [chicken wings out of a pile of wings](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/2023/01/19/isaac-soft-robotics-simulation/). Where does one wing start and end, though? And what’s the best way to grip a specific wing? It’s a challenging task. A pile of chicken wings can form an infinite number of positions or poses.

![Soft Robotics, for instance, worked with a food producer to create an AI solution that enables a robot to recognize and pick up single, wet and squishy chicken wings out of a pile of wings. ](https://www.controleng.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/CTL2401_WEB_IMG_A3_SoftRobotics_ChickenWings.jpeg)

Soft Robotics, for instance, worked with a food producer to create an AI solution that enables a robot to recognize and pick up single, wet and squishy chicken wings out of a pile of wings. Courtesy: A3, Soft Robotics

“This is where the superpower of simulation comes in,” said Gerard Andrews, senior product marketing manager for [robotics at NVIDIA](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/deep-learning-ai/industries/robotics/).

Rather than taking 10,000 pictures of all the ways chicken parts randomly drop, AI can build photorealistic, physically accurate 3D representations and put them under different lighting conditions, Andrews said. Using the images from the simulation to train the AI model saves time compared with photographing and labeling thousands of real-world images.

Data generated from computer simulations or algorithms is called “[synthetic data](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/2021/06/08/what-is-synthetic-data/),” Andrews explained.

“Using the synthetic data, Soft Robotics greatly accelerates how quickly companies can deploy robotic arms in different manufacturing applications to pick and place objects.”

## Using outlier cycle detection to double the throughput of a production line

AI also helps management focus their efforts. While factory floor supervisors can’t be everywhere at once, smart devices can. Eric Danziger, CEO at [Invisible AI](https://www.invisible.ai/), said ready-to-use smart devices help manufacturers uncover opportunities to optimize assembly lines.

Traditional cameras produce hours and hours of 2D video — and too much information.

“AI makes sense of the pictures and combines the visual input with other types of production data and signals to make a 3D map of people, their tools, current productivity, and cycle time,” Danziger said.

AI insight directs attention to where it’s needed. “AI helps you understand which thing your production team should pay attention to, such as a worker who quietly pushes a button repeatedly to get a balky machine to function but doesn’t alert a supervisor to the ongoing problem.”

Much of this comes down to a process at which Invisible AI excels: Anomalous cycle detection, which analyzes whether a human or machine cycle is performing within an expected range or abnormal.

A Tier 2 automotive supplier, for instance, doubled the throughput of a production line with Invisible AI’s help.

“They knew they had a problem line and needed better visibility and better views,” Danziger said. Using AI tools, they identified high spikes in cycle times at some stations, including the workstation shown in the shift management workflow chart below. Frontline operators and managers at the supplier now run shifts and find issues in real time.

![Using AI tools, they identified high spikes in cycle times at some stations. ](https://www.controleng.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/CTL2401_WEB_IMG_A3_ShiftManagement.jpg)

Using AI tools, they identified high spikes in cycle times at some stations. Courtesy: A3, InvisibleAI

In another case, an automotive OEM partnered with Invisible to identify underutilized stations, as shown in the process improvement workflow chart. The OEM used the insight to consolidate stations and produce 5% more per throughput per shift while reallocating 20% of headcount.

![An automotive OEM partnered with Invisible to identify underutilized stations, as shown in the process improvement workflow chart. ](https://www.controleng.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/CTL2401_WEB_IMG_A3_ProcessImprovement.jpg)

An automotive OEM partnered with Invisible to identify underutilized stations, as shown in the process improvement workflow chart. Courtesy: A3, InvisibleAI

## Ensure timely maintenance and quality control

Like a race car driver at a track, timely maintenance and faster pitstops can be a winning approach.

“Predictive maintenance is one of the first things to implement with AI in an industrial setting,” said Bernd Raithel, director of product management and marketing for factory automation at [Siemens Digital Industries](https://new.siemens.com/global/en/company/about/businesses/digital-industries.html).

Mechanical parts like bearings wear out and must be replaced routinely, like changing the engine oil in a car based on distance traveled.

“AI predicts that Machine A is going to fail with a stated confidence level in the next two days,” Raithel said, so the maintenance team knows to replace the bearings before they get stuck. A short, planned maintenance shutdown results in less loss of production than an extended, unplanned outage.

Prescriptive maintenance is a step beyond predictive maintenance. Although the two terms sound similar, prescriptive maintenance keeps more complex equipment running. AI may adjust the operations of the equipment to keep it going. And “prescriptive maintenance gives some ideas up front about what component is about to fail and what parts the technician needs to fix the machine,” Raithel said.

Successful AI requires data from production processes. When the public sees AI in action, the vendor has already performed the AI training. In contrast, for industrial manufacturers, the first step is to collect enough data on which to base decisions,” Raithel said. “There’s often a lot of data already available from machines.”

Siemens, for instance, used a wealth of production data to [increase throughput of a production line](https://www.controleng.com/articles/ais-revolutionary-impact-on-industrial-manufacturing/) of printed circuit boards by performing 30% fewer x-ray tests. They accomplished this task using AI to identify which boards were likely to benefit from inspection. The company collected large amounts of processes, parameters and other information about test results to feed the AI model as well as correlating 40,000 production parameters.

With the data, Raithel said, Siemens learned which parts were defective as well as the source of the defects, which the company used to further improve quality.

## Simulate new factories and processes with agility

New factory design and process changes involve risks that can be reduced through a 3D simulation in a type of virtual factory, otherwise known as a digital twin.

Linked to existing systems, a digital twin looks and works like the real-world factory it simulates. The industrial metaverse, a 3D virtual world built specifically for industrial manufacturers, makes this possible. These virtual environments also help to generate synthetic data to train AI/ML algorithms. In a recently announced partnership, NVIDIA and Siemens announced plans to [bring the industrial metaverse](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OXtJh1q6GxE) to industrial customers of all sizes.

![With simulation, the entire planning phase of the manufacturing facility can happen in a virtual world, and everything can be tried out and tested. ](https://www.controleng.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/CTL2401_WEB_IMG_A3_NVIDIA_BMWFactory.jpeg)

With simulation, the entire planning phase of the manufacturing facility can happen in a virtual world, and everything can be tried out and tested. Courtesy: A3, NVIDIA

A [FREYR virtual battery factory](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/2023/04/17/siemens-nvidia-freyr/), for instance, provides 3D representations of the infrastructure, plant, machinery, equipment, human ergonomics, safety information, robots, automated guided vehicles, and detailed product and production simulations.

A digital twin of a [BMW automotive factory](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g78YHYXXils#t=1m05s) is another example. With simulation, the entire planning phase of the manufacturing facility can happen in a virtual world, and everything can be tried out and tested. “The OEM knows with a high-level of confidence that a system is going to run and achieve the throughput on day one,” Andrews said.

From grasping chicken parts to building entire virtual factories, industrial manufacturers are using AI in the real and virtual worlds. The opportunities to increase agility and optimization through AI are (virtually) limitless.

– The [Association for Advancing Automation (A3)](http://www.automate.org) is a CFE Media and Technology content partner.

# The Top 10 Industrial AI use cases

December 6, 2019



[Hoang P](https://iot-analytics.com/author/hoang0701/)

IoT Analytics’ recently published the [Industrial AI Market Report 2020-2025](https://iot-analytics.com/product/industrial-ai-market-report-2020-2025). As part of the research, the analyst team identified a total of 33 different use cases that employ Artificial Intelligence tools and techniques on (predominantly) IoT-connected data sources and assets of industrial enterprises. These 33 industrial AI use cases have been grouped into 10 broader use case categories which make up the majority of the almost $15B Industrial AI market in 2019.

The top 10 ranked by size are:

## #1: Predictive maintenance

The largest use case for industrial AI is “Predictive Maintenance” (estimated to make up over 24% of the total market in 2018). Predictive Maintenance makes use of advanced analytics (e.g., Machine Learning) to determine the condition of a single asset or an entire set of assets (e.g., a factory).

The goal: Predict when maintenance should be performed. Predictive maintenance usually combines various sensor readings, sometimes external data sources, and performs predictive analytics on thousands of logged events. Predicting the remaining useful life of an asset using supervised ML is the most common technique in Predictive maintenance (see Exhibit 2).

![](https://mms.businesswire.com/media/20180606005083/en/661666/22/Predictive_Maintenance_Toolbox_can_help_train_predictive_models_that_can_estimate_remaining_useful_life_and_provide_confidence_intervals_associated_with_the_prediction.jpg)

**Exhibit 2:** An example of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction via regression ML technique. With the given failure threshold, an asset will most probably break in 9.5 days. Source: Mathworks, Image: [Businesswire.com](https://mms.businesswire.com/media/20180606005083/en/661666/22/Predictive_Maintenance_Toolbox_can_help_train_predictive_models_that_can_estimate_remaining_useful_life_and_provide_confidence_intervals_associated_with_the_prediction.jpg)

* **Example 1:** Deutsche Bahn, the German railway operator, leverages data from railway switches to predict failures, thus decreasing unexpected delays at scale. *Source*: [Konux Case Study](https://www.konux.com/wp-content/uploads/KONUX-case-study-weichenanalytik.pdf)
* **Example 2:** Nissan runs an AI Predictive maintenance platform to do RUL prognostication on 7,500 assets. The company claims an unplanned downtime reduction of 50% and a payback period of < 3 months. Nissan scaled the solution from 20 critical assets to thousands without increasing the workload of the on-site PdM team. *Source*: [Manufacturing.net](https://www.manufacturing.net/article/2018/08/how-ai-can-fill-maintenance-skills-gaps-boost-productivity)

One of the biggest challenges with Predictive Maintenance is the elimination of data imbalances as there is often not enough failure data for all the assets. Data is called imbalanced, when failure events represent less than some specific required share of the dataset. To make accurate predictions on the data, such imbalances have to be eliminated first. There are 2 main methods to achieve balanced data: data sampling and cost-sensitive learning algorithms.

## #2: Quality inspection & assurance

Quality inspection and quality assurance is the second largest industrial AI use case category at 20.5%. While there are various ways to do AI-based quality inspection, automated optical inspection is by far the largest sub-category.

Automated optical inspection is a technique where a camera autonomously scans the device under test for catastrophic failure (e.g. missing component) and/or quality defects (e.g. fillet size or shape or component skew). Computer vision is the foundation of optical inspection. Once the images are recognized, semi-supervised ML is the most effective technique to classify images into failure classes. The main benefit of this use case is cost reduction, and the main potential beneficiaries are large manufacturing facilities, where a small reduction in scrap or test time can yield very large savings.

Cost implications: after implementing optical inspection on one of its plants, BOSCH claimed to achieve $1.3M savings due to 45% of total test time reduction. *Source*: [BOSCH](https://bosch-connected-world.com/wp-content/uploads/BCW19_Breakout_Artificial_Intelligence_Rahul-Kapoor_Bosch.pdf).

* **Example:** A major German automotive company is introducing a deep learning-enabled system for quality control. This system is fully integrated into the flow of the final assembly process and thereby gets rid of the need to have a separate testing area in a controlled environment. The solution is expected to soon replace conventional camera booths that are used today and according to the OEM will result in “immense savings”.

## #3: Manufacturing process optimization

Perhaps the most obvious but still one of the most difficult to implement AI use cases is automated manufacturing process optimization. One implementation of this optimization is through Autonomous machines or robots.

The idea behind those autonomous assets is that they replicate monotonous human tasks in the manufacturing process, thus saving costs. Before being put into production, the autonomous machines/robots perform the same task over and over again, learning each time until they achieve sufficient accuracy. The reinforcement learning technique is often used to train robots and autonomous machinery. Under this technique, a robot can relatively quickly teach itself to do a task under the supervision of a human. The “brains” of such a robot/machine are usually neural networks.

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%200%200'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

**Exhibit 3:** A reinforcement learning system replicates the human natural learning process: an agent (e.g., a robot) takes an action, which is observed by an environment. A certain reward is generated and sent back to an agent. After repeating the process numerous times, a robot’s “brain”, i.e. a neural network, optimises behavior to satisfy the environment. Source: Mao, Alizadeh, Menache & Kandula (2016). Image source: [novatec-gmbh.de](https://www.novatec-gmbh.de/en/blog/deep-q-networks/)

* **Example**: ABB is investing $150M to build an “advanced, automated and flexible” robotics factory in Shanghai. In this plant, ABB will manufacture robots using robots. According to ABB, these robots will have autonomous and collaborative elements. The robots’ autonomy is built with the use of AI and digital twin. *Source*: [ABB.](https://new.abb.com/news/detail/9410/abb-to-build-the-worlds-most-advanced-robotics-factory-in-shanghai)

![](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%200%200'%3E%3C/svg%3E)

Image source: [Metrology.news](https://metrology.news/wp-content/uploads/2018/10/Robot-Making-Robots.png)

## #4: Supply chain optimization

8% of all industrial AI implementations are improvements to industrial supply chains. Using AI tools to improve inventory management is one of the key applications.

Predictive inventory management leverages predictive analytics for a variety of inventory-related tasks including to reduce inventory planning time, minimize inventory cost, optimize repairments, and find optimal reorder points.  For these tasks, techniques such as time-series analysis, probabilistic modeling (Markov and Bayesian models) as well as simulations (e.g., Monte-Carlo simulation) are most commonly used.

* **Example:** Continental has built software to predict the optimal points for tire changes on its fleet. The underlying model predicts the overall running mileage and compares it to the baseline, to generate actions. By that, Continental is reducing its stock of tires, also improving safety on the road.

## #5: AI-driven cybersecurity & privacy

AI-driven cybersecurity & privacy relates to aspects such as cyber threat detection. It typically involves observing the network infrastructure and detecting threats of cyberattacks in real time. It also often includes such activities as network traffic analysis, endpoint detection and response, malware sandboxes, etc. AI-powered cyber threat detection is often part of a larger cybersecurity solution that also uses a number of prevention measures (e.g., firewalls).

## #6: Automated physical security

Surveillance & physical threat detection entails real-time surveillance of manufacturing sites or workers in order to automatically detect physical security threats and/or potential safety hazards.

## #7: Automated data management

With data often stored in multiple systems and multiple places, it is hard to access and analyze the data quickly and holistically. Therefore, some industrial companies start to employ data management solutions that perform tasks such as data acquisition, data filtering, data cleaning & integration, etc. in real-time.

## #8: Smart assistants

Voice assistant is one of the examples of smart assistants in manufacturing settings. Integrating voice assistant technology into its real-time industrial monitoring systems allows workers to gain insights without coding the explicit commands or printing long status reports.

## #9: AI-driven research & development

Automated component design is the leading use case in AI-driven R&D. The goal: Letting software independently develop dozens of different designs in short periods, given a set of predefined constraints. The optimal design is chosen afterwards. For this task, digital twins and simulations often complement the AI techniques.

## #10: Autonomous resource exploration

Especially relevant in Mining & Quarrying and Oil & Gas industries, autonomous resource exploration is a technique of analysis and processing of the massive volume of images (e.g., radar, satellite or drone images) to detect the optimal point for resource extraction. AI can be especially useful in the detection of captivities in difficult-to-access areas, such as the ocean subsurface or mountains.

## More information and further reading

**Interested in learning more about the industrial AI market?**

The AI use cases discussed in this article are explored in much further depth, including a list of 100+ actual case studies, in the 146-page [Industrial AI Market Report 2020-2025](https://iot-analytics.com/product/industrial-ai-market-report-2020-2025).

The report also provides a technology overview, competitive landscape, deep-dive into benefits & challenges, a detailed market assessment, and implementation best-practices and trends.

IoT Analytics’ estimates the global industrial AI market size to reach $72.5B by 2025, up from just over $11B in 2018. The study, published in December 2019, also includes an industrial AI project database (110+ case studies), vendor list (300+ vendors) and market model data (38 tables) in Excel format.

d63.title: The most valuable AI use cases for business
d63.snippet:
Predictive maintenance remains a high-value industrial use case for AI, evolving from schedule-based maintenance into equipment health analysis. Machine learning AI models can identify subtle patterns that signal impending mechanical issues by continuously analyzing real-time data streams from IoT (Internet of Things) sensors and equipment logs. [...] AI allows robots to perform tasks that require perception, navigation and decision-making. In manufacturing and industrial settings, organizations increasingly deploy collaborative robots—or “cobots”—that safely work alongside human employees to streamline assembly, quality inspections and materials handling. [...] AI is transforming nearly every industry by helping organizations automate processes, improve decision-making and uncover new opportunities for growth. Applications vary by sector, but most organizations use AI to increase efficiency, reduce operational costs, use data more effectively and improve customer experiences.

# The most valuable AI use cases for business

Published 13 February 2024

Updated 03 June 2026

![Multi ethnic group of business people working all together in modern office](https://assets.ibm.com/is/image/ibm/6w1a3649?ts=1785346999576&dpr=off)

By [Matthew Finio](https://www.ibm.com/think/author/matthew-finio.html), [Amanda Downie](https://www.ibm.com/think/author/amanda-downie.html) and [Jim Holdsworth](https://www.ibm.com/think/author/jim-holdsworth.html)

[Artificial intelligence (AI)](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/artificial-intelligence) is evolving quickly. It wasn’t long ago that [generative AI](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/generative-ai) was drawing all the attention for its abilities to hold conversations, answer questions and create content. Now [agentic AI](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/agentic-ai) is making headlines for its abilities to make decisions, solve problems and accomplish goals with limited human supervision.

AI is being applied to an expanding range of business challenges and use cases. Across business functions and industries, teams are using AI to improve [customer experiences](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/customer-experience), increase productivity, [manage operations](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/ai-in-operations-management) and improve decision-making. While early AI initiatives often focused on automating routine tasks, today’s applications are helping businesses address more complex challenges and uncover new opportunities for growth.

The most successful AI initiatives tie to specific business objectives and measurable outcomes. As capabilities continue to mature, the range of practical AI business applications will expand. The following examples highlight valuable ways organizations are using AI to improve outcomes.

## Customer-facing AI use cases

### Customer experience

[AI improves customer experience](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/ai-customer-experience) by delivering more seamless and personalized interactions across the customer journey. AI systems analyze large volumes of customer data to help businesses better understand customer preferences, anticipate needs and tailor experiences in real time.

AI enables personalized recommendations that help businesses deliver relevant products, services and content. By integrating data across online, mobile, in-store and social channels, organizations deliver more consistent omnichannel customer experiences. This connectivity helps customers move seamlessly between touchpoints.

[Sentiment analysis](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/sentiment-analysis) evaluates customer feedback and identifies opportunities to improve satisfaction and loyalty. Many organizations also [incorporate AI into customer relationship management (CRM) systems](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/ai-crm) to automate routine tasks, improve decision-making and strengthen customer engagement.

### Customer service

[Customer service](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/ai-in-customer-service) remains one of the most common and valuable AI applications. Companies use AI to answer customer questions, resolve common issues and provide support across digital channels including websites, mobile apps, messaging platforms and contact centers. In fact, mature AI adopters (organizations operating or optimizing AI into their customer service functions) reported a 17% increase in customer satisfaction.1

Modern AI systems can understand natural language, access knowledge bases and guide customers through tasks that once required human assistance. Many businesses use [AI-powered customer service chatbots](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/ai-customer-service-chatbots), [virtual agents](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/virtual-agent) and [conversational AI](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/conversational-ai) systems built on [large language models (LLMs)](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/large-language-models) to provide 24/7 support.

[Contact center automation](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/contact-center-automation) and tools help customer service teams work more efficiently. Human agents use AI-powered agent assist tools to summarize conversations, retrieve relevant information, suggest responses and automate post-call documentation. These capabilities reduce administrative work and allow human agents to spend more time addressing complex customer needs.

When deployed effectively, AI helps organizations improve response times, reduce support costs and create more consistent customer experiences across channels.

Customer data has long informed business decisions. [AI allows organizations to take personalization much further](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/ai-personalization) by tailoring interactions, recommendations and content to individual users in real time.

Organizations use AI-driven personalization to deliver more relevant recommendations and experiences. [Recommendation engines](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/recommendation-engine) analyze purchasing history, browsing activity, product usage and other signals to identify relevant products, services and offers.

Personalization platforms can adapt content, recommendations and offers during customer interactions rather than relying only on predefined audience segments. AI can also help sales teams identify opportunities for cross-selling and upselling by highlighting products or services that complement existing customer purchases.

Retailers, streaming platforms, financial institutions and healthcare providers are just some of the organizations that use AI-powered personalization to better understand customer needs and deliver more relevant experiences. Effective personalization can improve customer satisfaction while increasing engagement, loyalty and conversion rates.

### Smart products and devices

AI is increasingly embedded within the devices people use every day. Smartphones, smart speakers, wearable devices, connected vehicles and home automation systems all rely on AI to improve functions and create more intuitive user experiences.

Product capabilities such as voice interaction, speech and language translation, image recognition, navigation, health monitoring and personalized recommendations are powered by AI. Many items incorporate on-device AI, which allows them to process information locally rather than relying entirely on cloud services.

For businesses, AI enables the development of smarter products and services. Manufacturers can use AI to improve device performance, adapt functions to individual users and deliver value to customers.
